I'm p4 with $553 and several unmortgaged properties. The offer is $200 cash for Kentucky and Indiana Ave. I'm weighing this against p3's dominant holdings.

Rejecting the offer is the better move. The red properties are mortgaged, so they cannot form a monopoly. Paying $200 would leave me with only $353 cash. That is too little to survive against p3's green monopoly rent of $1100.

Unmortgaging the red properties would cost roughly $231. Their base rent is only $36 combined, so the trade is not profitable. Handing over $200 would also strengthen p2 and help them rebuild their orange houses.

p2 has only $54 cash. Rebuilding orange houses would help damage p3, but that would also hurt me. I cannot afford to give them $200.

Re-mortgaging the red properties would not generate cash, since they are already mortgaged. I considered countering with p2's get-out-of-jail cards, but that would only help if I were sent to jail.

I will reject the trade outright. I will not counter or sweeten the offer. My public message will be brief and avoid revealing my cash fragility.
